questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about Article 129 of the Constitution of India?

options.text: It provides for the Supreme Court to give advisory opinion to the President.
It provides for the Supreme Court to be a court of original jurisdiction
It provides for the Supreme Court to be a court of record.
It provides for the Supreme Court to be the highest court of appeal.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **It provides for the Supreme Court to be a court of record.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 129** of the Constitution of India declares the Supreme Court to be a **court of record**. This status grants it two main powers: the power to punish for contempt of itself and the power to have its judgments recorded for perpetual memory and testimony.
 
• The option stating **"It provides for the Supreme Court to give advisory opinion to the President"** refers to **Article 143**, not Article 129, hence it is incorrect.
 
• The option that mentions **"It provides for the Supreme Court to be a court of original jurisdiction"** partially describes Article 131, which deals with the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court but does not fully encapsulate the provisions of Article 129. Therefore, it is not the best answer in this context.
 
• The statement about the Supreme Court being the **"highest court of appeal"** is true but is a more general characteristic of the Supreme Court and not specific to Article 129.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Supreme Court of India** has a wide range of functions and powers under the Constitution, including original jurisdiction, appellate jurisdiction, and advisory functions.
 
• As a **court of record**, the Supreme Court's judgments are of evidentiary value and cannot be questioned when produced before any court. They are recognized as legal precedents and sources of law.
 
• The role of the Supreme Court as the **highest court of appeal** covers appeals in civil, criminal, and constitutional cases, ensuring a unified interpretation of the law across India.

Hence, the statement about **Article 129** providing for the Supreme Court to be a court of record is correct

questions.question: Articles 29-30 of the Constitution of India deals with _______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Cultural and educational rights**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Articles 29-30** of the Indian Constitution specifically protect the rights of minorities, allowing them to preserve their language, script, and culture.
 
• These articles empower minorities to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice, safeguarding their educational rights.
 
• The provisions under these articles are crucial for maintaining the pluralistic fabric of Indian society by ensuring educational and cultural preservation.
 
• Article 29 provides that any section of the citizens residing in the territory of India or any part thereof having a distinct language, script or culture of its own shall have the right to conserve the same.
 
• Article 30 gives all minorities, whether based on religion or language, the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 

 Right to freedom
 Articles 19-22 deal with the right to freedom, including speech, assembly, movement, residence, and right to practice any profession.
 
 

 Right to equality
 Articles 14-18 ensure equality before the law and equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.
 
 

 Right to freedom of religion
 Articles 25-28 guarantee the freedom of religion and the right to practice, propagate, and profess any religion.

questions.question: Which of the following is connected with daily atmospheric weather changes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Troposphere**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The troposphere** is the lowest layer of Earth's atmosphere and is where nearly all weather conditions take place.
 
• It contains approximately 75% of the atmosphere's mass and extends from the Earth's surface up to about 8 to 15 kilometers (5 to 9 miles) high.
 
• **Temperature decreases** with altitude in the troposphere, which is why mountain tops can be snowy while it's warmer at sea level.
 
• **Weather phenomena** such as clouds, rain, snow, wind, and storms occur within this layer.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 

 Asthenosphere
 Located beneath the lithosphere, it's a semi-fluid layer that allows tectonic plates to move.
 
 

 Stratopause
 Marks the upper boundary of the stratosphere, located above the troposphere, not directly influencing daily weather.
 
 

 Lithosphere
 The rigid outer layer of the Earth, consisting of the crust and upper mantle, not directly involved in atmospheric weather.

questions.question: In which state is the famous Brihadeshwar temple situated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Tamil Nadu**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Brihadeshwar Temple** is located in Thanjavur, **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• It is also known as **Rajarajeswaram** or **Peruvudaiyār Kōvil**.
 
• This temple is a brilliant example of the major heights achieved in **Chola architecture**, painting, and bronze casting.
 
• The temple was built by **Chola emperor Raja Raja Chola I** in 1010 AD.
 
• It is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**, known for its architectural grandeur.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The **vimana** (temple tower) is 216 ft high and is among the tallest of its kind in the world.
 
• The temple has a massive **Shivalinga** in the main sanctum, which is a central figure in the worship practices there.
 
• One of the most astonishing features of the temple is the **shadow of the gopuram (tower)**, which never falls on the ground at noon during any part of the year.
 
• The walls of the temple are covered in detailed **bas-relief** and murals that tell various stories of Shiva, as well as other Hindu deities.

• The main temple tower, called the vimana, is usually a stepped **pyramid that rises geometrically.** Unlike the curving shikhara of North Indian temples, the vimana has a more angular, tiered appearance.
 
• Many Dravidian temples include a large** water reservoir or temple tank** within the complex, used for ritual purification.
 
• The temples are adorned with detailed carvings depicting various deities,** mythological scenes,** and floral patterns.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of capital receipt in the government budget?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Sale of government bonds**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Capital Receipts** are non-recurring by nature and include the funds received from the sale of fixed assets, borrowings, and the sale of government securities.
 
• **Sale of government bonds** is considered a capital receipt because it involves raising funds by borrowing from the public or institutions, which increases the government's liabilities.
 
• **Capital receipts** are distinct from revenue receipts, which are regular and recurring income sources like taxes and duties.
 
• The funds raised through capital receipts are often used for financing large-scale projects, investments, or to pay off existing debts.
 
• Capital receipts, including the sale of government bonds, do not recur regularly and do not form part of the regular income of the government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Type
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **Government Bonds**
 Debt securities issued by the government to finance its fiscal deficit, infrastructure projects, and other public expenditure.
 
 

 **Revenue Receipts**
 Regular income from taxes, fees, fines, and dividends from investments that do not lead to a liability or diminish an asset.
 
 

 **Deficit Financing**
 The practice of funding government spending by borrowing, leading to a fiscal deficit.
 
 

 **Public Debt**
 Total amount owed by the government to creditors within the country and abroad.
 
 

 **Fiscal Policy**
 Government policies regarding taxation and spending to influence the economy.

questions.question: Which of the following best defines transfer payments?

options.text: Payments made to individuals in exchange for their labour or services
Payments made by the government to individuals without any corresponding production of goods or services
Payments made by businesses to their shareholders as a share of profits
Payments made by individuals to the government in the form of taxes

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Payments made by the government to individuals without any corresponding production of goods or services.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Transfer payments refer to the sums of money distributed by the government to individuals without any goods or services being provided in return.
 
• These payments are essentially financial transfers from the government's funds to individuals, aiming to redistribute income and provide social benefits.Examples of transfer payments include unemployment benefits, welfare payments, and social security.
 
• Unlike taxes or purchases, these payments do not directly contribute to any economic production but are critical for supporting individuals who may be in need or less fortunate, thus maintaining economic stability and supporting social welfare

questions.question: Which is the Gaussian unit of kinematic viscosity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Stokes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gaussian units** are a system of physical units based upon the centimetre-gram-second (CGS) system of units. The Gaussian units for kinematic viscosity is **Stokes**.
 
• **Kinematic viscosity** is a measure of a fluid's internal resistance to flow under gravitational forces. It is expressed in terms of area per time, typically square centimeters per second (cm²/s).
 
• The **Stokes** (St) is the CGS unit of kinematic viscosity and is equivalent to cm²/s. It is named after George Gabriel Stokes, a British mathematician and physicist.
 
• Understanding kinematic viscosity is crucial in fields like fluid dynamics and aerodynamics, where the flow behavior of fluids is analyzed.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 

 Ampere
 The unit of electric current in the International System of Units (SI).
 
 

 Joule
 A derived unit of energy in the SI system, equivalent to the energy transferred when applying one newton of force over a distance of one meter.
 
 

 Darcy
 A unit of permeability used in the petroleum industry, which helps in understanding the flow of fluids through porous materials.
